The reaction is stereospecific, meaning that the stereochemistry of the reactants is preserved in the product. The reaction typically proceeds via a concerted mechanism, where the pi electrons of the diene and dienophile interact to form new sigma bonds. The reaction can be catalyzed by heat or Lewis acids, and the regioselectivity of the product can be influenced by substituents on the diene and dienophile. As a result of the reaction, a new carbon-carbon bond is formed, and the order changes from C=C to C-C, and from C=C to C-C as well. Note that the hints are describing the forward reaction, but you have to perform the retrosynthetic step.
